summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (53/71)

data.turoyo: Kəmmile: "Ya sidi! Ya u rabayḏan! Aḥna w an nošani nayar na, dəžmən, w qṭilan gawre m ḥḏoḏe, lə kməbnoyi.
data.translation: Sie sprechen zu ihm: "Herr! Wir und diese Leute sind Feinde, und wir haben uns gegenseitig Männer getötet, mehr, als man zählen kann.

rationale: Missing Detransitive Infectum box; uncountability of killed men. The modal reading is contextual, not a new sense.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1a in Infinitiv (94/354)

data.turoyo: Me d zbəṭle ḥa mənne, edi u ḥolo gnofəq mi ḥoluṯayḏe w hawo, d maxlaṣwayle bu bnoyo meqəm mu ḥreno, hawo kowe ḥolo edi.
data.translation: Wenn er einen von ihnen gefaßt hat, so verliert er seine "Onkeleigenschaft", und dann wird derjenige von den beiden, der beim abzählen zuerst "frei" wurde, "Onkel".

rationale: Missing Infinitiv box and new game-counting subsense; temporal b- action noun with role assignment.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.30/4761)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Lo bənanwo kmo noše kito b Tərkiya?
data.translation: Jan: Hadn't they counted how many people there are in Turkey?

rationale: First Preterit-wa proposal for counting homonym; preserve bənanwo as supplied and flag its suffix analysis for review. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New sense 1a: (mit ʕal-) count players out in a game

data.label: 1a
data.gloss: (mit ʕal-) count players out in a game

rationale: Repeated ʕal/reciprocal clauses assign game roles by the last number or counting word; words can replace numbers, establishing a specialized selection procedure.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC YT LIFE STORY/74)

data.turoyo: Uʕdo laq+qəryawoṯani dəbneli kulle xəd Baǧənne, xəd K̇avnā́s, xəd K̇očane, xəd Daywank̇e, xəd Ṫaqá ŭ Xarabya, aṯən kul+ḥa, kmaʕmarle bote. <...>
data.translation: Now these villages that I counted, all of them, like Bacin, like Kefnas, like Koçan, like Denwan, like Taqa and Harapya, everyone came back, (everyone) was building houses. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; enumeration of named villages and clear separation from subsequent building.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 39/16)

data.turoyo: Qayəm ṣafro u paša, bnele aw waze, naqiṣi ḥḏo.
data.translation: Am Morgen stand er auf und zälte die Gänse, sie waren wieder um eine weniger geworden.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; goose-counting with a quantitative deficit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 44/40)

data.turoyo: <...> Gbonenən knufqi šawʕo, krəxawno kowən əšto. <...>
data.translation: <...> ich zäle sie, so ergeben sich sieben, ich sitze auf, dann sind's nur sechs. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell and unusual contracted object suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 86/24)

data.turoyo: <...> Lo qədrət bonət ag garme di lašayḏe. <...>
data.translation: <...> du kannst die Knochen seines Körpers nicht zählen; <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; active modal inability rather than a new counting sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/312)

data.turoyo: <...> annaqlla u yawmo bu yawmo kobənyo, hawi ʕumre arbʕi yawme, aṯyo əmmo: "Tux larke!"
data.translation: <...> Sie zählt die Tage, tagfür Tag. Als er vierzig Tage alt war, kam sie und sprach: Komm her! -

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; feminine repeated counting of days.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 73/11)

data.turoyo: Əmmi: "Gbənena aṣ ṣafure." Omər: "Bnawunne." Bnanne, naqiṣi ʕəsri.
data.translation: "Wir wollen erst die Zicklein zälen", antworteten jene. "Zält sie nur!" Als sie dieselben zälten, waren zwanzig zu wenig da.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell; plural command with plural object suffix, contrasted with Infectum and Preterit in one verse.

summary: example for sense 1a in Infectum (94/345)

data.turoyo: Ḥa mənne gbone hul l aʕ ʕəsri aʕlayye. U ḥa, towe ʕəsri, hawo komaxləṣ.
data.translation: Einer von ihnen zählt sie aus bis zwanzig. Der, auf den die Zwanzig fällt, wird frei "aus".

rationale: New game-counting subsense; ʕal participants and explicit selection at twenty.

summary: example for sense 1a in Infectum (94/348)

data.turoyo: W a tre ḥrene ste gbonən ʕal ḥḏoḏe, u ḥa, d oṯele aʕ ʕəsri, hawo meqəm mu ḥreno yaʕni gmaxləṣ.
data.translation: Die letzten beiden zählen sich wieder aus, und der, auf den die zwanzig fällt, wird später früher als der andere "frei".

rationale: New subsense; reciprocal ʕal ḥḏoḏe construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Jan 2.5/1219)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Kmo buġre kito bu tarʕo du ḥəmmam maḥyo, ḥuru! Bnawu dukṯe d kul buġro!"
data.translation: He says, 'How many bullets are there, shot into the bathhouse door? Look! Count the mark of every bullet!'

rationale: Imperativ I.1 remains thin after round 1 (three examples); plural Bnawu counts bullet marks in a self-contained command. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.31/4851)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: E. U Faġro yo, i Qandelo yo, u Ṣṭəʕraf yo, u Zəwoġo yo, eeeee, u Murən yo, hedi klay d bənenox, u ḥreno mən yo?..
data.translation: Father Brahim: Yes. There is the Body, there is the Qandelo [anointing of the sick], there is confession, there is marriage, eeeee, there is chrism; wait, let me count them for you, what is the other one?...

rationale: Unusual bənenox with recipient reference in an explicit sacrament list is better contextualized than the bare 'count them for me' request. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: The counting homonym remains bny2 throughout. Named villages and numerical objects distinguish it from bny1 build despite identical base forms.
Enumeration without a numerical result is already present in the existing sweet-things example; village names do not require a new sense. Days, coins, livestock and bones are participant extensions.
Negated Detransitive Infectum and Infectum-wa express countability rather than necessarily an actual counting event. Preserve singular məbne and plural məbnoyi/məbnan forms.
Counting-out selects players by a terminal number or word; reciprocal ʕal-government recurs across the game descriptions. New1a keeps existing sense1 and its examples unchanged.
All new added glosses use the entry’s English; edition German and English examples retain their supplied wording.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; quoted English is copied from the supplied machine translation.
All eighteen tokens belong to the counting homonym, not bny1 build. Jan's metadiscursive name-list requests do not establish a new 'mention' sense.
Round-1 I.1 Preterit and Infectum already have five examples each; reader thin-cell counts predate that round and are not reused. The game-counting subsense1a receives no Jan support here.

bunenən, boneno, bunatli, bənatlan, bənatline, bənenox and bonatte show source variation and multiple pronominal dependents. Recipient l- should be distinguished from the counted item; suffix segmentation is not reconstructed from English.
kibox introduces an ability request and is not another occurrence of this root. The census is institutional counting, not a technical lexical sense.
105/71 has an alignment warning: German adds removal of the objects outside the supplied Turoyo. Its translation is not quoted; compare source boundaries before adding it.
PrS39/9 German does not render Bnanne, naqiṣi; no translated example is added from that occurrence.
53/15 German omits the tents clause. Obtain an aligned edition rendering before quoting the full coordinated Turoyo example;53/71 supplies the new box instead.
Resolve Gbənanne in PrS39/3 and object/agent segmentation of Bnanne, bonətte and bonalle; box assignment is provisional where suffixes alone are opaque.
Compare11/135 source bnalle with glossary bnalli and105/63 bnalla with105/71 bnalle; preserve witnesses rather than make an unverified fix-text.
Confirm active Infinitiv placement for bnoyo; the form differs from Detransitive məbne and no Detransitive voice is claimed.
Confirm bənanwo in2.30/4761 as Preterit-wa rather than a reduced Infectum-wa or another form; the English anterior tense alone is insufficient, and the new example preserves the uncertainty.
Segment bunenən, bənatline and bənenox against the counted plural and recipient. Does boneno in1.47/2092 have an omitted object or a contracted object suffix?
Confirm bnelox ad dukkanaṯṯe in1.16/607 as listing the shops from preceding discourse; the isolated form is homonymous with 'build'.
Correct “in inneren” to “im Inneren”.
rationale: The preposition/article should be im, and the German noun requires capitalization. The supplied edition reads “Im inneren”.

summary: Names, weddings, tailors, priests, sacramental items, vessels and census populations are ordinary counting/enumeration. Listing without a numerical total already belongs to sense1 and was reinforced in round 1.
